# Japan Travel Kit

> Practical, independent planning guides for foreign visitors to Japan: eSIMs and mobile data, trains and rail
> passes, money and payment cards, and attraction tickets. Written in English for people who have not been to
> Japan before, and aimed at the decisions you have to make before you land.

Operated by mjo Inc., a Japan-based company in Tokyo working in inbound tourism and e-commerce consulting.

How the facts on this site are sourced, because it matters for quoting them:

- Prices, fares and admission rules are read off the operator's own site — the railway, the venue, the card
  issuer, the eSIM provider — and each page states the date it was read.
- Where a resale or booking platform is the practical route for a visitor (a foreign card the official site
  rejects, an English checkout), the page says so and links to it. Those links are affiliate links and are
  disclosed on every page that carries one.
- Nothing on the site is written as a first-hand trip report. The guides describe what the operators publish
  and what follows from it, not visits we claim to have made.
- Full method and company details: https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/about

## Start here

- [All guides, indexed by topic](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides): every guide on the site, grouped by the question it answers.
- [Japan Attraction Ticket Prices 2026](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/japan-attraction-ticket-prices): one table of official adult and child admission, advance-booking rules, operator sources and check dates for 19 Japanese attractions, theme parks, passes and day-trip sites. Most recent check: 28 October 2026.
- [eSIM & SIM Cards hub](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim): Japan is one of the easiest countries in the world to get online in: there is no SIM registration for visitors, and every tourist eSIM rides one of the three national carriers — Docomo, SoftBank or KDDI — so coverage is rarely what separates them.
- [Transport & Getting Around hub](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport): Japanese transport splits into two layers that barely overlap. Long-distance travel between cities runs mostly on JR, where the question is always the same: individual tickets or a pass. Inside a city it is subways, private railways and buses, where a tappable IC card handles almost everything and day passes only pay off on heavy days.
- [Money & Payment hub](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money): Japan has a reputation for being cash-only that is roughly a decade out of date — cards and IC cards now work in most city shops, restaurants and convenience stores. What has not changed is that small businesses, shrines, local buses and rural areas often still take cash only, and that most foreign cards are refused by most Japanese ATMs.
- [Things to Do hub](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions): A handful of Japan's best-known attractions cannot be bought at the gate. teamLab, Tokyo Disney, Universal Studios Japan and the Shibuya Sky sunset slots all sell date- and time-specified tickets online, and the popular slots go weeks ahead — in Disney's case, with no same-day sales at all.

Getting online in Japan. 21 guides covering which eSIM to buy, how to install one, the unlimited plans, and the pocket WiFi and physical SIM alternatives. Plan prices are refreshed from the providers' own sites by a scheduled job and each table carries its own check date.

- [Cheapest eSIM for Japan 2026: Best Budget Picks](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/cheapest-esim-japan): Don't overpay for data in Japan. We compared eSIM Go, Airalo, Holafly, and Sakura Mobile on price per GB — prices checked daily.

We compare Holafly, Sakura Mobile, and Airalo on true unlimited vs large data plans — including which ones are unlimited in name only.
- [Airalo vs Holafly for Japan (2026): Which Should You Choose?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/airalo-vs-holafly-japan): Both are popular Japan eSIMs — but they suit very different travellers. We compare price, data, coverage and support head-to-head with a clear verdict.
- [Japan SIM Card vs eSIM (2026): Which Should You Choose?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/japan-sim-card-vs-esim-2026): eSIM for almost everyone, from $3.99 — but there are exactly two situations where a physical SIM is the only option, and price has nothing to do with either of them: a Japanese phone number, and a handset with no eSIM hardware.
- [Pocket WiFi vs eSIM for Japan (2026): Which Is Better?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/pocket-wifi-vs-esim-japan): Both keep you connected in Japan — but one is cheaper, simpler, and needs no hardware. We compare price, convenience, and coverage so you can choose.

The rentals are near-identical on data and network, so the choice is device limit and whether it meets you at the airport or at your hotel.
- [Best eSIM for Japan Reddit (2026): Which Advice Still Holds](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/best-esim-japan-reddit): r/JapanTravel recommends the same four eSIMs every time. We check each claim against this month's prices — three hold up, and one is badly out of date.
- [Airalo Japan Review 2026: Is It Worth It?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/airalo-japan-review): Airalo's Japan eSIM plans, networks, and setup process — plus whether it really works nationwide. An honest verdict on pricing, coverage, and who it's best for.

- [Sakura Mobile Review 2026: eSIM & SIM Card Plans and Prices](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/sakura-mobile-review): Unlimited on au or 3 GB a day on docomo, as an eSIM or a SIM card you collect at the airport. Plan prices in yen, the hotspot limit, and the one plan that comes with a Japanese phone number.
- [eSIM Go Japan Review 2026: Prices, Networks and Tethering](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/esim-go-japan-review): The cheapest Japan eSIM at every tier we track, on docomo and SoftBank, with tethering stated on every plan at no extra cost. What you give up: no phone number, no in-app top-up, email support only.
- [How to Set Up an eSIM in Japan (Step-by-Step)](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/how-to-set-up-esim-japan): Install your Japan eSIM before you fly and have 4G the moment you land. Step-by-step for iPhone, Android, iPad and Android tablets — plus a full troubleshooting section.
- [Best eSIM for Japan on iPhone (2026): Japan eSIM iPhone Setup & Picks](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/japan-esim-iphone): Which Japan eSIM installs cleanly on an iPhone, and exactly where to tap in iOS. - [Does eSIM Work in Japan? (2026): Everything You Need to Know](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/does-esim-work-in-japan): Yes — on Docomo, SoftBank or au/KDDI, with no SIM registration and no ID check. - [Best Japan eSIM for 2 Weeks (2026): Plans That Last the Trip](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/japan-esim-2-weeks): Almost nobody sells a 14-day plan, so the usual mistake is buying on allowance and landing on one that expires at day 7. Every plan filtered by validity, cheapest first.

- [Japan eSIM for Family & Group Travel (2026): Cost Per Head](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/esim/japan-esim-family-group): An eSIM each or one shared Pocket WiFi? It is arithmetic, and on today's prices it turns over at two people. With the per-person cost of both, read from live prices.

## Transport, rail passes and airport transfers

Trains, passes and airport runs. 14 guides covering whether the Japan Rail Pass still pays after the 2023 price rise, IC cards, the shinkansen, city-by-city transport, and the airport routes into Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto, with official fares.

- [JR Pass Guide 2026: Prices, Is It Worth It and How to Buy](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/jr-pass-guide): All pass types and prices, a break-even calculator for your own route, and how to buy and redeem the pass — plus the itineraries where individual tickets cost less.
- [Shinkansen Guide 2026: Tickets, Passes & Tips for First-Timers](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/shinkansen-guide): Japan's bullet train is fast, punctual, and easy to use — once you know how. We cover ticket types, prices, JR Pass tips, and how to book before you board.
- [Tokyo to Kyoto (2026): Cheapest & Fastest Ways to Get There](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/tokyo-to-kyoto): The Shinkansen is fast but not always the cheapest. We compare the bullet train, highway bus, local trains, and rental car on price, speed, and comfort — with 2026 fares.
- [Tokyo to Kanazawa (2026): Kagayaki Times, Seats and Whether a Pass Pays](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/tokyo-to-kanazawa): 2h28m direct on the Hokuriku Shinkansen, no transfer — and the Kagayaki has no non-reserved car at all. With the ¥35,000 Hokuriku Arch Pass against the ¥50,000 JR Pass, and the Tsuruga change for Kyoto and Osaka.
- [Tokyo Airport Transfer Guide (2026): Narita & Haneda to the City](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/tokyo-airport-transfer): N'EX, Skyliner, limousine bus, or taxi? We compare every way to get from Narita or Haneda airport to central Tokyo — with a Skyliner vs N'EX head-to-head and when the bus wins.
- [Tokyo Airport Limousine Bus (2026): Narita & Haneda Fares, Times and Stops](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/tokyo-airport-limousine-bus): A fare per route, not per airport: ¥3,600 Narita to Shinjuku, ¥2,900 to the Disney resort, ¥1,400 from Haneda. With the two-bag hold rule, which routes need a reserved seat, and the ¥2,800 late-night bus.
- [Osaka Airport Transfer Guide (2026): KIX & ITM to the City](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/osaka-airport-transfer): Osaka has two airports — Kansai International and Itami. We compare every way to get into the city from each, with a Haruka vs Nankai Rapi:t head-to-head.
- [Haruka vs Nankai Rapi:t (2026): Best Train from Kansai Airport?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/haruka-vs-nankai-rapit): One runs to Namba, the other to Tennoji, Shin-Osaka and Kyoto — so your hotel decides this, not the fare. A head-to-head on time, price, and JR Pass coverage.
- [Getting Around Tokyo (2026): Trains, Subway & IC Cards Explained](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/tokyo-transportation): Tokyo has the world's most complex train network — but once you know the basics, it's easy. We cover the Yamanote Line, Tokyo Metro, IC cards, the Tokyo Subway Ticket, and key routes for every tourist destination.
- [Getting Around Kyoto (2026): Buses, Trains & Taxis Explained](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/kyoto-transportation): Kyoto's city bus and subway cover nearly every major sight. We explain how each option works, which IC card to use, when the Subway & Bus day pass pays off, and how to arrive from Tokyo or Kansai Airport.
- [Getting Around Osaka (2026): Subway, Trains & IC Cards Explained](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/osaka-transportation): Osaka's subway system is one of the easiest in Japan to navigate. We cover the Midosuji Line, the Enjoy Eco Card vs Osaka Metro Pass, IC cards, and key routes to top attractions.
- [IC Cards in Japan 2026: Suica, Pasmo & How to Use Them](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/ic-cards-japan): An IC card is the single most useful thing you can have in Japan. Here's everything you need to know about Suica, Pasmo, where to get them, and where they work.
- [Osaka Metro Pass 2026: Price, 1-Day vs 2-Day & Enjoy Eco Card Compared](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/osaka-metro-pass): The 1-day Osaka Metro Pass is ¥820, or ¥620 at weekends and ¥310 for children. The two-day option is now a ¥1,200 30-hour pass. With pick-up points and the buses it skips.
- [Is the Kyoto Subway & Bus 1-Day Pass Worth It? (2026)](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/transport/kyoto-subway-bus-pass): Great value on a temple-hopping day, a waste on a quiet one. We show where the break-even falls — and why the old ¥700 bus pass you may have read about no longer exists.

## Money, cards and payments

Paying for things. 13 guides covering cash versus card, which ATMs take foreign cards, the travel cards worth holding, currency exchange, tax-free shopping and what a trip actually costs.

- [Wise vs Revolut for Japan (2026): Which Travel Card Wins?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/wise-vs-revolut-japan): Wise or Revolut for Japan? We compare exchange rates, weekend fees, ATM limits, and plans — with clear advice on which card suits your spending.
- [Best Travel Card for Japan (2026): Fees and ATM Limits Compared](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/best-travel-card-japan): Debit, prepaid and credit compared on card cost, foreign transaction fees, exchange rate and Japanese ATM fees — plus which card to carry from the US, UK, Australia, Canada and the Eurozone.
- [Wise Card in Japan (2026): ATM Fees, Free Limits & Which ATMs Take It](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/wise-card-japan): Yes, the Wise card works at Japanese ATMs. Free withdrawals to 250 USD/GBP/EUR or 400 AUD a month, then 2.69% — plus the ¥220 Japan Post Bank adds per use.
- [Revolut in Japan (2026): Fees, ATMs & Is It Worth It?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/revolut-card-japan): Does Revolut work in Japan? We break down the plans, weekday and weekend FX fees, ATM limits, and whether Revolut is worth it for your trip.
- [Cash vs Card in Japan (2026): Where Cards Work and Where You Need Yen](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/cash-vs-card-japan): METI puts Japan's cashless share at 58.0% of consumer spending — and yet temples, market stalls and local buses still want yen. Place by place, what each operator says it takes.
- [ATMs in Japan (2026): Which Accept Foreign Cards & What the Fees Are](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/atms-in-japan): Five ATM networks take a card issued abroad — Seven Bank, Japan Post Bank, E-net, Lawson Bank and AEON — and only one publishes its fee. Brands, fees, hours and limits compared.
- [Currency Exchange in Japan (2026): Best Ways to Get Yen](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/currency-exchange-japan): Where you exchange your money makes a big difference. We rank the best options from 7-Eleven ATMs to airport counters — and explain which to avoid to get the best yen rate.
- [Contactless Payment in Japan (2026): What Actually Works](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/contactless-payment-japan): Japan runs three contactless systems and they are not interchangeable — your tap-to-pay Visa will not open a ticket gate. Which tap works where, and why you should skip QR pay.
- [Tax-Free Shopping in Japan (2026): The ¥5,000 Rule and the New Airport Refund](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/tax-free-shopping-japan): ¥5,000 before tax per shop per day, on a non-resident passport. From 1 November 2026 the 10% comes back at an airport customs terminal instead of at the till — here is the official procedure.
- [Japan Travel Budget 2026: Trip to Tokyo Japan Cost & How Much Things Cost](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/japan-travel-budget): What a trip to Tokyo costs and how much things cost in Japan, built only out of published prices: a ¥178 subway ride, a ¥420 bowl of ramen, official admissions, the three cities' lodging-tax bands, and 3 to 14-day totals.
- [Best Travel Insurance for Japan 2026: Cover and Cost](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/best-travel-insurance-japan): Heymondo, SafetyWing and World Nomads on their own published limits and prices — SafetyWing from US$62.72 per 4 weeks, Heymondo cover to $10,000,000 — set against the ¥7.5m and ¥10m treatment cases JNTO publishes.
- [SafetyWing vs Heymondo for Japan (2026): Which Should You Pick?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/safetywing-vs-heymondo-japan): Subscription vs trip cover for Japan. We compare medical limits, app support, ski cover, and waiting periods so you know which insurer fits your trip.
- [Best Travel Insurance for Skiing in Japan (2026): Off-Piste, Rescue Costs and What Is Covered](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/money/japan-ski-travel-insurance): On-piste skiing is standard cover; off-piste is excluded on every SafetyWing plan, add-on included. Compared on published policy wording — plus the ¥100,000 minimum Niseko charges for a backcountry rescue.

## Attraction tickets, theme parks and passes

Official ticket prices and booking rules for the attractions that sell date- and time-specified tickets — teamLab, Tokyo Disney, Universal Studios Japan, the observation decks and the city passes. Every price on these pages is the operator's own, with the date it was read off their site.

- [Japan Attraction Ticket Prices 2026: Official Prices and Booking Rules](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/japan-attraction-ticket-prices): Official adult and child admission for every ticketed attraction, park, pass and day-trip site we have verified — in one table, each row dated and sourced to the operator's own site.
- [teamLab Planets Tickets (2026): Prices, How to Book & Planets vs Borderless](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/teamlab-tokyo-tickets): Official Planets prices, the 30-minute entry slots, opening hours and what to wear for the barefoot water areas — plus how Planets differs from Borderless in Azabudai.
- [teamLab Borderless Tickets (2026): Price, How to Book and Time Slots](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/teamlab-borderless-tickets): Adult admission from ¥3,400 on the official site and priced by date and slot, how the timed Entrance Pass and the Flexible Pass differ, hours and closed days, and whether to book direct or through Klook.
- [Shibuya Sky Tickets 2026: Price, Hours & Sunset Slots](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/shibuya-sky-tickets): ¥2,700 online for an adult entering before 15:00 and ¥3,400 after, ¥300 more at the 14F counter — plus the hours, the two-week booking window, and which slot actually sells out.
- [Tokyo Tower Tickets (2026): Prices, Main Deck vs Top Deck & How to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-tower-tickets): Main Deck admission is ¥1,500 and costs the same at the door; only the ¥3,300 Top Deck Tour is cheaper booked online. Plus the 23:00 closing that no other Tokyo deck matches.
- [Tokyo Joypolis Tickets (2026): Passport Prices, Hours and Height Limits](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-joypolis-tickets): Admission alone is ¥1,700 and the all-ride Passport ¥6,000 for an adult, with a cheaper Evening Passport from 15:00 — and thirteen of the twenty-one rides have a minimum height.
- [Tokyo Disneyland Tickets 2026: Prices, Rules & DisneySea](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-disney-tickets): A 1-Day Passport starts at ¥8,900 for an adult and is priced by date. No gate sales at either park, your date opens two months ahead at 14:00 JST, and refunds do not exist — but the date can be changed.
- [Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan Tickets (2026): Prices, Hours and Time Slots](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/osaka-aquarium-kaiyukan-tickets): The admission moves by date — ¥2,700 to ¥3,200 for an adult — and the e-ticket books a 15-minute entry slot from 30 days out. Plus the hours, the walk from Osakako, and the re-entry rule that ended in June 2026.
- [Umeda Sky Building Tickets (2026): Prices, Hours and the Best Time to Go](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/umeda-sky-building-tickets): ¥2,000 for an adult and ¥500 for a child aged 4 to elementary school, with the 173 m rooftop open 9:30–22:30 and last entry at 22:00. Plus Osaka sunset times by season and the 15:00 cut-off on the Amazing Pass.
- [Osaka Castle Tickets (2026): Prices, Hours and What the Pass Covers](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/osaka-castle-tickets): The main tower is ¥1,200 and about 60 minutes, open 9:00–18:00 with last admission at 17:30. The four other paid facilities inside the park total ¥5,200 — which is why the city pass wins here.
- [Universal Studios Japan Express Pass 2026: Types, Prices & Do You Need One](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/usj-tickets-express-pass): Express Pass 4 and 7, what each covers, why the price changes with your date, when the day's allocation sells out, and the dates a Studio Pass on its own is enough.
- [Sanrio Puroland Tickets (2026): Prices, Variable Pricing & How to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/sanrio-puroland-tickets): An adult Day Passport runs ¥3,900 to ¥6,900 depending on the date, so choosing the day saves more than choosing the seller — and the park also requires a separate arrival reservation.
- [Fuji-Q Highland Tickets (2026): Free Pass Prices, the Q Pack & How to Get There](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/fuji-q-highland-tickets): Entry to the coaster park at the foot of Mt. Fuji is free; the 1-Day Pass is ¥6,000 to ¥7,900 by date, and the Q Pack bundles it with the round-trip highway bus from Tokyo.
- [Sumo in Tokyo (2026): Tournament Tickets vs Morning Practice](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/sumo-tokyo-tickets): The 2026 Tokyo tournament dates, how to buy official tickets safely (and avoid resale sites), seat types and same-day tickets, plus year-round morning practice tours.
- [Tokyo Skytree Tickets (2026): Prices, Floor 350 vs 450 & How to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-skytree-tickets): Official prices for Floor 350 and the Floor 450 combo, the ¥500 service fee the same-day counter adds, and why buying the skywalk up front is cheaper than adding it on site.
- [Warner Bros. Studio Tour Tokyo Tickets (2026): Prices & How to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/warner-bros-studio-tour-tokyo-tickets): Official prices for the Harry Potter studio tour in Nerima, what the Afternoon Tea packages actually add, the four hours to allow, and how to reach Toshimaen.
- [Tokyo Subway Ticket (2026): 24, 48 or 72 Hours — Is It Worth It?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-subway-ticket): The 24/48/72-hour prices from Tokyo Metro, the break-even worked against official single fares, and the exclusion that catches people out — JR, including the Yamanote Line.
- [Tokyo Observation Decks (2026): Shibuya Sky vs Skytree vs Tokyo Tower](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-observation-decks): Four decks compared on height, official price and what you actually see from each — including the Metropolitan Government Building, which charges nothing at all.
- [Japan 14-Day Itinerary (2026): 2 Weeks in Japan, Day by Day](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/japan-14-day-itinerary): Four bases rather than seven — Tokyo 5 nights, Kawaguchiko or Hakone 1, Kyoto 4 with Nara, Osaka 3 — with a table for each of the fourteen days and official prices for every ticketed stop, dated.
- [Japan 10 Day Itinerary (2026): 10 Days in Japan, Day by Day](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/japan-10-day-itinerary): Nine nights on three hotel bills — Tokyo 4, Kyoto 3, Osaka 2 — with a Hakone day that ends on a westbound train and a Nara day trip, plus a table for each of the ten days and the JR Pass worked against what this route actually uses.
- [Osaka 2 Day Itinerary (2026): Day by Day, and What to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/osaka-2-day-itinerary): The castle and Minami on Day 1, the bay and Umeda on Day 2, joined by 20 minutes of Midosuji Line — with a table for each day, the ¥3,500 of Day 1 admissions a ¥2,500 pass covers, and the one stop that has a fixed entry slot.
- [Tokyo Kyoto Osaka Itinerary (2026): 7 Days in Japan, Day by Day](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-kyoto-osaka-7-day-itinerary): The first-visit route in a week — Tokyo 3 nights, Kyoto 2, Osaka 1, out from Kansai — with a table for each of the seven days, the shinkansen and local-train times, and what has to be booked before you fly.
- [Tokyo 5-Day Itinerary (2026): 5 Days in Tokyo, Day by Day](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-5-day-itinerary): Three city days plus Kawaguchiko and Kamakura, with a table for each of the five days, published journey times for every leg out of the city, and only five bookings that have to be made ahead.
- [Tokyo 3 Day Itinerary (2026): What to Book, and in What Order](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-3-day-itinerary): Three days, three districts — west, east and centre — with a table per day and only two stops that need a timed ticket. Official prices for each ticketed stop, with the date we checked them.
- [Things to Do in Tokyo (2026): What to Book Ahead and What to Walk Into](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/things-to-do-tokyo): A short list of the Tokyo attractions that need a timed ticket weeks out, and the ones you can turn up to — so your booking effort goes where it is actually needed.
- [Things to Do in Kyoto (2026): Temples, Timing and What to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/things-to-do-kyoto): Kyoto's headline sights are mostly walk-in, which changes how you plan a day there. What needs reserving, what does not, and how to fit the big three together.
- [Things to Do in Osaka (2026): Where the Pass Pays and Where It Doesn't](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/things-to-do-osaka): Osaka rewards a pass more than most Japanese cities, with one large exception — Universal Studios Japan, which no pass covers.
- [Kimono Rental in Japan (2026): Kyoto vs Asakusa and How Booking Works](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/kimono-rental-japan): Rental is a half-day commitment with a fixed return time, not a costume hire. How the dressing appointment works, and which city suits it better.
- [Kyoto Kimono Rental (2026): Which Area, What's Included, When to Return](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/kyoto-kimono-rental): The decision is the area, not the shop: Gion and Kiyomizu put you inside a 25-minute walking route, Arashiyama is a self-contained day, Kyoto Station is a changing room. Plus the 17:30 same-day return.
- [Dotonbori River Cruise (2026): Price, Times, Pier and the Pass](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/dotonbori-river-cruise): ¥2,000 for an adult, about 20 minutes, and a departure every half hour from Tazaemonbashi Pier between 11:00 and 21:00 — free on the Osaka Amazing Pass if you exchange the voucher before the evening boats fill.
- [Japanese Tea Ceremony Experience (2026): Tokyo, Kyoto and What to Expect](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tea-ceremony-japan): A beginner session runs under an hour and is led in English at most listings aimed at visitors. What the session covers, and how Kyoto and Tokyo differ.
- [Samurai and Ninja Experience in Tokyo (2026): Sword Lessons, Where to Go and Tickets](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/samurai-ninja-experience-tokyo): Museum visit, armour-wearing session or sword lesson — three different things sold under one name, and the one worth booking depends on who you are going with.
- [Tokyo Street Go-Kart (2026): Rules, IDP Requirement and How to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-go-kart): Street go-karting in Tokyo needs a Japanese licence or a valid International Driving Permit, and an IDP has to be issued before you leave home. Everything else is detail.
- [Tokyo Food and Izakaya Tours (2026): Shinjuku Bar Hopping and What to Eat](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-food-tour): A guided crawl buys you into the small places you would not walk into alone — the izakaya counters and Golden Gai bars that look closed to outsiders.
- [Tokyo Night Food Tour (2026): Omoide Yokocho, Golden Gai and the 20+ Rule](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-night-food-tour): About three hours through Omoide Yokocho, Kabukicho and Golden Gai — roughly 280 bars that mostly open around 20:00, and the drinking age of 20 that decides who can come.
- [Osaka Food Tour (2026): Which One to Book, Times and What You Eat](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/osaka-food-tour): The Shinsekai evening runs 17:30–20:30 with five eateries, 15 dishes and 3 drinks; the Dotonbori walk is 11:00–14:00. One replaces dinner, the other lunch — you only need one.
- [Tokyo Bay Cruise (2026): Yakatabune vs the Symphony, Times and Prices](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-bay-cruise): Two different boats are sold under one search term. The Symphony sails four times a day from Hinode Pier with a boarding-only ticket from ¥1,800; a yakatabune is 2 to 2.5 hours from ¥13,000 with dinner.
- [Tsukiji Market Food Tour (2026): Hours, What to Eat and Which Tour to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tsukiji-market-food-tour): The outer market trades 9:00 to 14:00, many shops close on Sundays and some Wednesdays, and buyers have priority until 9:00. Plus why the tuna auction is at Toyosu, not here.
- [Asakusa Kimono Rental (2026): Return Times, Hair Sets and Where to Photograph](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/asakusa-kimono-rental): A half day with a hard edge: the outfit is due back at 16:30 or 17:30 depending on when you arrived, and the appointment itself takes 45 to 60 minutes before you step outside.
- [Tokyo Cooking Class (2026): Sushi and Ramen Making — What to Expect](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-cooking-class): Hands-on classes in English run a couple of hours and send you home able to repeat the dish. How to pick between sushi, ramen and the market-shop formats.
- [Osaka Amazing Pass (2026): ¥2,500 a Day — Is It Worth It?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/osaka-attractions-pass): Official 1-day and 2-day prices, what the 40-plus free admissions actually include, and the two attractions everyone assumes are on it that are not.
- [Hakone Free Pass (2026): Prices, What It Covers & Is It Worth It?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/hakone-free-pass): Odakyu's official prices — ¥7,100 for 2 days from Shinjuku, ¥6,000 from Odawara — the eight modes of transport it covers, the ¥1,200 Romancecar surcharge it does not, and why there is no 1-day version.
- [Kansai Area Pass (2026): Prices, What It Covers & Is It Worth It?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/kansai-area-pass): JR West ended sales of the old pass on 30 September 2026; the WEST QR version is ¥2,700 for 1 day to ¥6,700 for 4. What it covers, the Haruka rules, and the itineraries that pay it back.
- [Sagano Romantic Train Tickets (2026): Prices, Seats & When It Runs](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/sagano-romantic-train-tickets): ¥880 adult and ¥440 child one way for 7.3 km and 25 minutes up the Hozugawa gorge. The 2026 season, the two-month winter shutdown, the one-month booking window and the boat back down.
- [Where to Stay in Tokyo (2026): Best Areas, Compared by Line and Airport](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/where-to-stay-in-tokyo): Shinjuku, Tokyo Station, Ueno/Asakusa, Shibuya and Ginza compared on the lines under them — the Romancecar's 80 minutes to Hakone, the Skyliner's 41 to Keisei-Ueno, 23 minutes from Haneda to Higashi-ginza. No hotel names and no rates, because neither can be verified.
- [Where to Stay in Osaka (2026): Best Areas, Compared by Line and Airport](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/where-to-stay-in-osaka): Namba, Umeda, Tennoji and Universal City compared on the lines under them — the Rapi:t's 34-minute minimum from Kansai, 30 minutes to Kyoto on the JR Special Rapid, 36 to JR Nara from Tennoji, and a five-minute walk to the USJ gates.
- [Where to Stay in Kyoto (2026): Best Areas, Compared by Line and Travel Time](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/where-to-stay-in-kyoto): Kyoto Station, Karasuma Oike, Gion and Arashiyama compared on the lines under them and the official minutes to the four sights — Fushimi Inari 10, Arashiyama 25, Kiyomizu-dera 35, Kinkaku-ji 40. Plus the lodging tax bands in force since 1 March 2026.
- [Ghibli Park Tickets (2026): Prices, When They Go On Sale and How to Buy From Overseas](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/ghibli-park-tickets): The Standard O-Sanpo Day Pass is ¥3,300 on a weekday and the Premium ¥7,300, with no gate sales at all — tickets open two months ahead on the 10th at 2 p.m. Japan time, from the only two sellers the park names.
- [LEGOLAND Japan Tickets (2026): Prices, Hours and Is It Worth It?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/legoland-japan-tickets): The operator's online rates start at ¥4,900~ for an adult and ¥3,700~ for a child aged 3 to 18 and vary by date, the park is built for ages 2 to 12, and it is 24 minutes and ¥360 from Nagoya Station on the Aonami Line.
- [Matcha Experiences in Japan (2026): Uji, Kyoto and Tokyo Tea Houses Compared](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/japan-matcha-experiences): Uji is 16 minutes from Kyoto Station on the JR Nara Line, and it is where you can grind tencha on a stone mill (3h30m) or pick leaves in Wazuka. Plus the Kyoto and Tokyo tea houses, from 45 minutes up.

## Day trips and day tours

Whole days out of Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka, where the decision is which itinerary rather than which ticket: Mt. Fuji, Hakone, Nikko, Kamakura, Nara and Hiroshima, independently or by guided coach.

- [Mt. Fuji Day Tour From Tokyo (2026): Which Tour, and What You Actually See](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/mt-fuji-day-tour-from-tokyo): Every tour stops at the Subaru Line Fifth Station — what separates them is whether the rest of the day is Fuji or Hakone, and how long you will sit on a coach.
- [Hakone Day Trip From Tokyo (2026): Freepass Prices vs a Day Tour](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/hakone-day-trip-from-tokyo): Odakyu's official Freepass prices, the eight modes of transport it covers, the Romancecar surcharge it does not — and why there is no 1-day version of the pass.
- [Kyoto and Nara Day Tour From Osaka (2026): Which Itinerary to Book](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/kyoto-nara-day-tour-from-osaka): Four itineraries compared on which half of Kyoto they cover, how long the day runs, and whether Todai-ji's ¥800 Great Buddha Hall admission is in the price.
- [Mt. Fuji Day Trip From Tokyo (2026): How to Get There Yourself](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/mt-fuji-day-trip-tokyo): The independent route to Kawaguchiko by highway bus or limited express, what the Mt. Fuji Pass covers once you are there, and the season with the best odds of a clear summit.
- [Nikko Day Trip From Tokyo (2026): Getting There, Costs and Whether to Take a Tour](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/nikko-day-trip): Two hours north of Tokyo for Toshogu and Kegon Falls. How the Tobu and JR routes differ, how long the day runs, and when a guided coach beats doing it yourself.
- [Kamakura Day Trip From Tokyo (2026): Great Buddha, Hase-dera and the Fares](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/kamakura-day-trip): The easiest day trip out of Tokyo — about an hour on a JR line a rail pass already covers, with official admissions for Kotoku-in and Hase-dera.
- [Nara Day Trip (2026): From Osaka or Kyoto, and What Todai-ji Costs](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/nara-day-trip): Nara is the short day trip in Kansai — well under an hour from either city. The deer park is free; the Great Buddha Hall is ¥800, and that is the fee tours differ on.
- [Hiroshima and Miyajima Day Trip (2026): Is One Day Enough?](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/hiroshima-miyajima-day-trip): Two UNESCO sites in a day, and the honest answer on whether to attempt it from Kyoto or Osaka — plus Itsukushima Shrine's ¥300 admission and the Mt. Misen ropeway fare.
- [Kawaguchiko Day Trip From Tokyo (2026): Routes, Fares and What Fits in a Day](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/kawaguchiko-day-trip-from-tokyo): The north shore of Lake Kawaguchi is about 1 hr 45 min and ¥2,200 from Shinjuku by bus. Official fares for the ropeway, the lake boat and the sightseeing bus — and why a day holds two or three stops, not five.
- [Karuizawa Day Trip From Tokyo (2026): Shinkansen Times, the Five Stops and Tour vs DIY](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/karuizawa-day-trip-from-tokyo): The shortest mountain day trip out of Tokyo — 60 to 75 minutes on the Hokuriku Shinkansen, or ¥2,600 and about 3 hr 20 min by Seibu bus. Plus the tourism association's own one-day bus course, and why three stops is a realistic day.
- [Kobe Day Trip from Osaka (2026): Routes, the Beef and What Fits in a Day](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/kobe-day-trip-from-osaka): About 30 minutes to Sannomiya on any of three railways. Kitano's Weathercock House ¥500, the Port Tower ¥1,200 open to 23:00, the Rokko Cable Car ¥1,550 return to 21:00 — and why the Kobe beef table is the only thing that sells out.
- [Arima Onsen Day Trip (2026): From Osaka or Kobe, and What the Baths Cost](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/arima-onsen-day-trip): 65 minutes and ¥1,400 by coach from Osaka Station, 30 minutes and ¥780 from Sannomiya. Kin no Yu ¥800, Gin no Yu ¥700, and the closed Tuesdays that do not overlap.
- [Himeji Castle Day Trip (2026): ¥2,500 Admission, and Times From Osaka & Kyoto](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/himeji-castle-day-trip): 1 hr 1 min from Osaka by special rapid, 28 minutes from Shin-Osaka by shinkansen. Admission went to ¥2,500 on 1 March 2026 and under-18s are free — plus the 16:00 last entry and the 1,000-an-hour cap on the keep.
- [Tokyo Illuminations 2026: Dates, Hours and Which Ones Are Free](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/tokyo-illumination-tours): Ten Tokyo displays whose operators have announced the 2026–27 season — Marunouchi, Keyakizaka, Tokyo Midtown, Tokyo Dome City, Yebisu and the two ticketed ones — with the opening and closing nights, the lighting hours and the date we checked each.
- [Takayama and Shirakawa-go Tour (2026): Which Departure, and the Bus If You Go Alone](https://www.japan-travel-kit.com/guides/attractions/takayama-shirakawago-tour): Nagoya is about 11 hours, Kanazawa 8–10 with an English guide, Takayama 7h20m. With Nohi Bus's ¥2,800 fare and 50 minutes, the reserved ¥2,800 bus from Kanazawa, and the four reservation-only 2027 light-up evenings.
